title: UK FCA Issues 2026 Regulatory Priorities Mandating AI Governance and Accountability
article_content:
The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) has published its Regulatory Priorities Reports for 2026 for the Wholesale Markets and Wholesale Buy-Side sectors. The reports outline a pivot to a more outcomes-focused supervisory model, emphasizing the \"safe and responsible adoption of new technology.\" For 2026, the FCA explicitly expects firms to implement robust governance for emerging technologies by establishing clear accountability, risk management, and oversight for the use of AI and Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT). 

Specifically, wholesale market participants must improve third-party and technology risk oversight through robust due diligence when integrating AI into trading controls and liquidity frameworks. For the Buy-Side, the FCA is focusing on strengthening governance frameworks to manage the firm's impact on markets, with a particular focus on effective risk management of investment models and strategies that employ AI. The regulator also announced that it will continue to collect information via surveys in Q2 2026 to understand the maturity of firms' insider risk management regarding AI-driven data.

additional_sources.title: FCA Regulatory Priorities 2026 reports for Wholesale Markets and Buy-Side firms
additional_sources.article_content: The FCA’s original reports provide the primary regulatory language behind the Linklaters analysis and are useful because they show the issue is not just commentary but an explicit supervisory expectation. The documents emphasize governance, senior accountability, technology resilience, third-party oversight and risk controls when firms adopt AI or DLT. They also place AI in a broader market-integrity framework, linking model governance to liquidity management, trading controls, and the fair functioning of markets. That official wording is complementary for newsletter writing because it provides regulatory precision and confirms that AI governance is becoming a concrete compliance requirement rather than an abstract best practice.

market_context_source.title: Global regulators tighten expectations for AI use in financial services as governance moves from principles to supervision
market_context_source.article_content: This broader market-context source shows the FCA is not acting in isolation. International supervisory bodies are converging on a common view that AI in finance must be governed through board-level accountability, model-risk management, third-party oversight, operational resilience and clear human responsibility for outcomes. The BIS perspective is useful because it frames the FCA’s 2026 priorities as part of a cross-border regulatory shift from high-level innovation support toward concrete supervisory scrutiny of how AI is embedded in trading, surveillance, risk, and client-facing processes. That wider context helps explain timing and significance: firms are facing an environment where local regulation, global supervisory coordination and rising dependence on external technology vendors are all increasing the cost of weak AI governance.
